newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia stocks close slightly up as golds soar.
newsitem.headline: Australia stocks close slightly up as golds soar.

text.p: *Shares close off highs, but gold stocks soar after heavy sell-off this week. Rest of market mixed. Vol 313.05 million, value A$728.97 million, 1,095 stocks traded, 286 steady, 518 up, 291 down.
Australian shares closed slightly firmer on Friday, with gold stocks rebounding after this week's heavy sell-off. But the market finished the week weaker due to precious metal's continuing woes.

At 4.10 p.m. (0610 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 4.7 points up at 2,699.1, but off its morning high of 2,703.7, while the September share price index futures was steady at 2,710, narrowing the premium to 10.9 points on the physical index.
Traders said the market steadied in afternoon trade as local investors took positions ahead of Friday's U.S. June Producer Price Index, which may set the tone for Wall Street.
Brokers said there was buying opportunties in local gold stocks, which have fallen over 20 percent during the past week until this morning, while the bullion price had dropped around five percent.

"You would definitely have to say they (gold stocks) have found support," said Tim Phillips, investment director at Tyndall Investment Management. Phillips said Normandy seemed to be the most favoured gold stock to buy into.
Normandy, Australia's largest gold miner, topped the turnover charts with over 17 million shares traded and its share price rising 10 percent to A$1.54.
Sipa Resource shares plunged over 50 percent after it announced results that showed its Mount Olympus gold prospect was not viable.

In other markets, Australian bond yields edged up as the market squared-up ahead of the weekend and in front of the U.S. PPI data later on Friday. At 5.05 p.m. (0705 GMT), the 10-year T-bond was five percentage points up at 6.69 percent.

At the same time, the Australian dollar was trading at US$.7440/45, compared with Thursday's close of $0.7425/30. The dollar posted its strongest close for the week as investors covered short positions made in case of a interest rate cut.
